title: Split generic component cover and uniform upper bound after shrinking
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $S$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and put $k=\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Fibres are scheme-theoretic [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There exist a field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], whose spectrum map $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is finite (its coordinate algebra is a finite module) and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], an integer $n\geq0$, and an open subset $W\subseteq S$ containing $\eta$, with the following properties. The scheme $G=X_\eta\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product] has exactly $n$ distinct irreducible components $A_1,\ldots,A_n$, which cover $G$. For every $i$ and every field extension $E/L$, the inverse image of $A_i$ in $G\times_{\operatorname{Spec}L}\operatorname{Spec}E$ is irreducible and nonempty. For every $s\in W$ and every field extension $K/\kappa(s)$, the scheme $X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}K$ has at most $n$ irreducible components. The case $n=0$ is allowed: the displayed component list is empty and all the indicated fibres over $W$ are empty. No flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good), proof: paragraph 2 (generic field splitting) and final paragraph (finite closed component cover gives the geometric upper bound); retained parent Steps 2--3.

proof.text: The generic fibre $X_\eta$ is finite type over $k$ by base change. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-components-split] to obtain $L/k$ and its finite etale spectrum map $a$ such that every component of $G$ has irreducible nonempty inverse image after every extension of $L$. By base change again, $G$ is finite type over $L$. The field $L$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] to enumerate the distinct components of $G$ as $A_1,\ldots,A_n$. They are closed by [def-weil-irreducible-components], and cover $G$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. This proves all the generic-data clauses; if $n=0$, that cover says $G=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good), generic splitting paragraph; Tag 0551 (lemma-make-components-generic-fibre-geometrically-irreducible), field-extension construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-geometric-generic-cover-spread] with the finite index set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and precisely the $L,a,A_i$ of Step 1. Its hypotheses hold: $f$ is finite type, $S$ is irreducible, $a$ is finite etale, the $A_i$ are a finite closed cover, and their inverse images under every field extension are irreducible and nonempty. It gives an open $W$ containing $\eta$. For any $s\in W$ and any $K/\kappa(s)$, put $Y=(X_s)_K$. The conclusion supplies a surjective scheme morphism $p:Z\to Y$ and irreducible nonempty subsets $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ covering $Z$. We use no assertion about their intersections.

source.place: Tag 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good), final paragraph; Tag 055G (lemma-geometrically-connected-generic-fibre), closure-and-shrinking construction, before the connectedness conclusion.

proof.text: Set $C_i=\overline{p(B_i)}\subseteq Y$. Each $C_i$ is nonempty and irreducible: in any closed two-set cover of $C_i$, inverse images under the continuous map $p|_{B_i}$ cover $B_i$, so one contains $B_i$; the corresponding closed set then contains $\overline{p(B_i)}$. Surjectivity and the cover by the $B_i$ imply $Y=\bigcup_i C_i$. For an irreducible component $D$ of $Y$, the finitely many relatively closed sets $D\cap C_i$ cover $D$. Repeatedly apply the two-set definition of irreducibility (induction on $n$) to get $D\subseteq C_i$ for some $i$. Since $C_i$ is irreducible, maximality of $D$ gives $D=C_i$. Assign each component the least index realizing this equality; different components have different assigned indices. Hence there are at most $n$ components. If $n=0$, the empty cover gives $Z=\varnothing$, and surjectivity gives $Y=\varnothing$. Since $s,K$ were arbitrary, these are exactly the required upper bound and empty-fibre clauses.
